date: 27 Oct 1513 ("In Vagliadulit", closing on the verso)
title: Francesco Guicciardini, Florentine ambassador in Spain, Valladolid, 27 October 1513: about 40 lines of sign cipher in three long blocks, bare, endorsed as deciphered
correspondents: Francesco Guicciardini (signed "Fr. de Guicciardinis Dr. Ambasciator"), Valladolid -> Lorenzo di Piero de' Medici
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza CXXXVII, doc. 619 (c. 627)
folio_note: c. 627r: clear opening (5 lines), then three blocks of dense sign cipher (Greek-like and Latin-like letters, E, C, ω, with superscript digits 1-3 over many signs), about 40 lines in all, separated by clear sentences ("V. M.tia che e prudentissima ...", "non voglio dire questo ..."); c. 627v: one cipher line at the top, clear closing, address. Head of c. 627r in a contemporary hand, hard to read: "Decifrata ... la copia prec.te"?
status: Bare (1272 px): no interlinear clear text. The head note seems to say it was deciphered, but the neighbours are not a decipherment (617 blank leaf, 618 a short clear letter of 4 Oct 1513; 620 Corsi's letter of the same day).
why: A cipher despatch of Guicciardini from his Spanish legation, written to Lorenzo the year the Medici returned. His legation letters are printed (Canestrini, Opere inedite VI, 1864; Jodogne, Le lettere), very probably from his own clear minutes in the Archivio Guicciardini, so the clear text may well be in print: check before any work.
verify: Look up the letter of 27 Oct 1513 to Lorenzo in Jodogne, Le lettere I-II, and Canestrini VI; if it is printed, the pair gives the key for the Corsi row; if not, transcribe and solve (homophonic sign cipher with superscript indices).
prior_art: Probably printed from Guicciardini's own minutes (not checked in this run). known.py: no hit on the document.

title: Giovanni Corsi, Florentine orator at the court of Ferdinand the Catholic, Valladolid and Madrid, Oct 1513 - Apr 1514: four letters and three contemporary copies with bare letter-and-figure cipher
correspondents: Giovanni Corsi (signed "Jo. Cursius or.", "Joannes Cursius or. apud Cath. M.tem", "Giovanni Corsi") -> Lorenzo di Piero de' Medici
language: Italian (letter/figure cipher with superscript indices between clear words)
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza CXXXVII, docs. 620 (c. 628 bis), 621 (c. 629, copy of 620), 622 (c. 630, copy of a letter of 29 Jan 1514), 623 (c. 631 bis), 627 (c. 635?), 628 (copy of 627), 633 (c. 641, copy)
folio_note: 620 (Valladolid 27 Oct 1513): about 16 cipher lines in two blocks on c. 628 bis r, one on the verso; 621: "Copia di lettera de 27 oct. 1513 da Vagliadulit", the same cipher text (about 18 lines); 622: copy of a letter of 29 Jan 1514 (about 11 lines); 623 (dated "xvi ... 1513", st. fior. = early 1514): about 22 lines in four blocks; 627 (Madrid, 25? Dec 1513): about 7 lines; 628: "Copia" of 627 with an added clear paragraph; 633 ("Copia", Madrid 9? Apr 1514): about 15 lines. Signs are lower-case letters (a, b, d, e, f, g, k, m, o, t, x, y, z) and digits 3-9 with superscript indices, some code groups (R, gg, aba, 1519, 1814) and repeated whole groups between clear words.
status: Bare (1272 px on 620, 623, 627, 633; 800 px on the copies): no interlinear gloss and no filed decipherment beside any of them (the copies repeat the cipher, they do not decipher it).
why: A run of cipher despatches from the Florentine embassy to Spain in 1513-14 (the Holy League, the Swiss, the truce with France), with duplicate ciphertexts (620/621, 627/628) for checking a transcription; about 90 cipher lines in all. The same superscript-index style is glossed in CXXXVII 626 and 636 (keys.json) and in the 1513-15 MAP LXXII pairs (Acciaiuoli, Pandolfini).
verify: Transcribe 620 and 621 together; test the glossed 626/636 tables and the LXXII Acciaiuoli 190/191 and Pandolfini pairs; check the Guicciardini row for a printed clear text of the same week; then a homophonic solver on all seven.

date: Florence, May 152[0 or 1] (733: "Florentiae ... Maij M.D.XX."; 734: "Floren. xv Maij MDXX.", last numeral unclear)
title: Cardinal Giulio de' Medici (the future Clement VII) to Galeotto de' Medici in Rome, May 1520/21: two letters wholly in two different sign ciphers, bare
correspondents: Card. Giulio de' Medici, vice-chancellor (large autograph signature "V. Jul. vicecancell."; the same as on doc. 735, Rome 19 July 1523) -> Galeotto de' Medici, Rome
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza CXXXVII, docs. 733 (c. 741) and 734 (c. 742)
folio_note: 733 c. 741r: after "Ven. nobis dilect.", a whole page (about 28 lines) of geometric signs (squares, crosses, T-shapes, circles, loops, dotted and double-dotted signs) evenly spaced; c. 741v: about 14 more lines, then clear closing, date and signature. 734 c. 742r: after "Mag.ce vir amice mi char.me", about 14 lines of a different alphabet (3, x, D, φ, square, U, B, 6, 8, z-like signs), "Ben valete Floren. xv Maij MDXX.", signature; address on c. 742 bis v to Galeotto de' Medici in Rome.
status: Bare (1272 px on both rectos; 800 px on the versos). Neighbours 732 and 735 are clear letters; no decipherment filed beside them.
why: Outgoing cipher of Cardinal Giulio, who ran Florence and the Medici foreign policy for Leo X, to the family's orator in Rome, in the year of the imperial alliance (May 1521). verify: Read the year at full size (Giulio was vice-chancellor until Nov 1523); transcribe 734 first (short alphabet, word spacing absent) and solve as monoalphabetic with homophones; then 733.
